Q699416.label: 1940 United States presidential election
Q699416.summary: Presidential elections were held in the United States on November 5, 1940. The Democratic ticket of incumbent President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Secretary of Agriculture Henry Wallace defeated the Republican ticket of businessman Wendell Willkie and senator Charles McNary, to be re-elected for an unprecedented third term in office. Until 1988, this was the last time in which the incumbent party won three consecutive presidential elections.

He was a moderate conservative with a strong intellectual reputation, but became a weak prime minister at the start of the worldwide Great Depression.

Q55832.label: Bolesław Bierut
Q55832.desc: Polish politician and leader of Poland (1947–1956)
Q55832.summary: Bolesław Bierut was a Polish communist activist and politician who was the leader of communist-ruled Poland from 1948 until 1956. He was President of the State National Council from 1944 to 1947, President of Poland from 1947 to 1952, General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Polish United Workers' Party from 1948 to 1956, and Prime Minister of Poland from 1952 to 1954. Bierut is believed to have worked as an NKVD informant or agent prior to 1945, although his relationship with the Soviet agency has been a subject of debate among historians.

Q137907736.label: 2026 Italian constitutional referendum
Q137907736.img: Italian ballot paper for 2026 constitutional referendum (front).svg
Q137907736.summary: A constitutional referendum concerning the reform of the judicial system was held in Italy on 22 and 23 March 2026. Its purpose was to revise Title II and Title IV of Part II of the Italian constitution. It was the fifth constitutional referendum in the history of the Italian Republic.

Q207384.label: Alexander I of Yugoslavia
Q207384.desc: Prince regent of Kingdom of Serbia and later King of Yugoslavia 1921–34
Q207384.img: Propriété d' Albert Kahn , Boulogne , France S .A .R Alexandre , Prince Régent du Royaume des Serbes , Croates et Slovènes.jpg
Q207384.summary: Alexander I Karađorđević was King of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes from 16 August 1921 to 3 October 1929 and King of Yugoslavia from 3 October 1929 until his assassination. His thirteen-year reign was the longest of the kingdom's three monarchs. He served as the de facto head of state of the Kingdom of Serbia from 1914 to 1918 and of Yugoslavia from 1918 to 1921 as prince regent for his father, Peter I.

Q1267224.label: 1994 Finnish presidential election
Q1267224.summary: Presidential elections were held in Finland on 16 January 1994, with a second round on 6 February. It was the first time the President had been solely and directly elected by a popular vote. Martti Ahtisaari defeated Elisabeth Rehn in the second round.

Q310296.label: Independent Social Democratic Party of Germany
Q310296.wiki: Independent Social Democratic Party of Germany
Q310296.summary: The Independent Social Democratic Party of Germany was a short-lived, left-wing political party in Germany during the late German Empire and early Weimar Republic. It was established in 1917 by members of the Social Democratic Party of Germany (SPD) who opposed Germany's involvement in World War I. After much of the USPD's membership joined the Communist Party of Germany (KPD) in 1920, the remainder returned to the SPD in 1922, with the exception of an insignificant faction that lasted until 1931.

Q930328.label: United Democrats
Q930328.summary: The United Democrats is a liberal political party in Cyprus. The party was founded by former President of Cyprus George Vasiliou in 1993 as Kinima Eleftheron Dimokraton. The party later merged with ADISOK to form United Democrats. The party is a full member of the Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe and an observer member of the Liberal International.

Q2605592.label: Communist Party of Moldavia
Q2605592.summary: The Communist Party of Moldavia was the ruling and sole legal political party of the Moldavian SSR. It was one of the fifteen republic-level parties that formed the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU) until the fall of the Soviet Union in 1991. During World War II, it was the driving force of the Moldovan resistance against Axis occupation.
